solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicatorNotes.tuning: tuning adjusts and rearranges an engine, so the letters get reworked

annotation.surface: A motorist, perhaps from the continent, souping up an old Ford Cortina.
annotation.walkthrough: The Cortina was a popular British family Ford of the 1960s and 70s; the car is just a bag of letters here.
annotation.definitionFit: A Croatian is a native of Croatia, a European country.

indicatorNotes.makes appearance in: the answer shows up inside the next word

annotation.surface: A religious sighting reported in the Cheshire town of Runcorn.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'Jesus' as an exclamation of surprise, not the man; Cor! is the British equivalent. Runcorn is an industrial town in Cheshire.
annotation.definitionFit: Both 'Jesus!' and 'Cor!' are exclamations of astonishment.

indicatorNotes.delivered in: the training is placed inside the talk

blocks.note: to orate is to talk formally
PE = physical education, school training; goes after the O

annotation.surface: A work training course given as a spoken presentation.
annotation.walkthrough: PE is physical education, the school gym lesson.
annotation.definitionFit: A machine that works operates.

entries.clue: Snacks, milk and a slice of salami (5)

indicatorNotes.a slice of: just a sliver, the opening letter, of salami

blocks.note: to milk a source is to tap it

annotation.surface: A plate of bar nibbles: dairy and some cured sausage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Milk' looks like the drink but is the verb, to exploit or draw off.
annotation.definitionFit: Tapas are small Spanish snacks served with drinks.

entries.clue: Roman general with a hold over father (7)

annotation.surface: An ancient commander who has some power over his own father.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' just places the first pieces above PA. Marcus Agrippa was Augustus's general, victor at Actium.
annotation.definitionFit: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa was a leading Roman general.

blocks.note: a fluffy Chinese breed with a blue-black tongue
informal, originally army slang for grub

annotation.surface: A label on a tin of pet food.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one thing, dog food, but splits into two separate definitions: the chow chow breed and chow as slang for grub.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a named dog breed from China, and a slang word for grub that came from pidgin English.

entries.clue: Try old wine mostly and become happy (7)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, the last letter dropped

blocks.note: TENT, an old name for a Spanish red wine, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone sampling vintage wine and cheering up as they drink.
annotation.walkthrough: Tent is an archaic word for a dark Spanish wine, rarely seen outside crosswords. 'Try' is the courtroom sense, not taste.
annotation.definitionFit: To hearten can mean to take heart, cheer up.

annotation.surface: A wan, ghostly person losing weight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thinner' looks like a comparative adjective but is the noun: the solvent used to thin paint.
annotation.definitionFit: White spirit is the British name for a paint thinner (mineral spirits).

indicatorNotes.primarily: first in line, so the opening letter

annotation.surface: Hoodlums who are sorry for coming clean.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the first word is cut down; 'regret' contributes a whole synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a true friend or a true account is honest, faithful to the facts or to a person.

entries.clue: A pinko brat upset office temp? (10)

indicatorNotes.upset: knocked over, letters thrown into disorder

annotation.surface: A spoilt young leftie throwing a tantrum at the agency temp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Office temp' sounds like a temporary worker; it is a temporary office. A Portakabin is the British brand of portable prefab building used on sites.
annotation.definitionFit: A Portakabin often serves as a temporary office, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: A stack battered over time in storms (7)

indicatorNotes.battered: beaten out of shape, so rearranged

blocks.note: T = time, added to the mix

annotation.surface: A pile of something knocked about during bad weather.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Storms' is the verb, as troops storm a fort, not the weather the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: To storm a position is to attack it.

blocks.note: a break is a run of scoring pots at snooker
pauses from work, as a noun

annotation.surface: A snooker player who would like the cue rests on the table.
annotation.walkthrough: In snooker a rest is the stick that props the cue, a tempting false lead; here rests are simply pauses.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a scoring visit to the table in snooker, and a pause such as a tea break.

entries.clue: Basic ingredients cooked up alarm waiter (3,8)

annotation.surface: A kitchen scene where the dish frightens the person serving it.
annotation.walkthrough: The restaurant surface makes 'ingredients' look like food, but the answer is the general phrase for inputs to any process.
annotation.definitionFit: Raw material is the basic stuff from which things are made.

entries.clue: Oscar-holding group on about those in MASH? (8)

indicatorNotes.holding: the group-on pair holds O inside it

blocks.note: NATO alphabet; sits between POTAT and ES

annotation.surface: A film reference to the Korean War comedy M*A*S*H and its Academy Award.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals are a disguise: MASH is not the TV show but mashed potatoes, and Oscar is just the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: Potatoes are what goes into mash, with the question mark flagging the wordplay on MASH.

indicatorNotes.undersized: cut short, so the last letter is lost

blocks.note: PEAK with its final K removed

annotation.surface: An adorable little mountaineer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mountain climber' reads as one phrase, but the split falls between them: the climber is a plant.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this scented garden flower grows up canes by tendrils, so it is one of many climbers.

indicatorNotes.blocking: stands in the way, so sits inside

blocks.note: to exit life is to pass on
I = one; goes between PASS and ON

annotation.surface: Someone furiously standing in a doorway to stop people leaving.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exit' is a euphemism for dying, as in 'pass on'. The question mark flags anger as one example of a passion.
annotation.definitionFit: Passion is strong emotion, especially rage.

indicatorNotes.outfitted: dressed in the cape, so placed inside it

blocks.note: the cape is the superhero's garment
kept as is; follows the knight inside CAPE

annotation.surface: A caped crusader and a knight lounging on the settee.
annotation.walkthrough: The obvious canapé is a party nibble; the definition uses its older French sense of a sofa.
annotation.definitionFit: A canapé is also an ornate sofa.

blocks.note: chemical symbol; goes between DAN and ES

annotation.surface: Scandinavians shipping in coal, or perhaps footballs.
annotation.walkthrough: Balls look like the round sort; they are formal dances.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the formal-party sense: a hunt ball or a charity ball is a grand social evening of dancing.

indicatorNotes.in: the core letter goes inside the error

blocks.note: a cock-up is British slang for a blunder
middle letter of fiLed; goes after the first C

annotation.surface: A document mistakenly put in the wrong folder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Record' is the verb, as a car clocks up miles, not a filed document. Cock-up is everyday British for a mess-up.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from the mileage clock: a driver who logs a distance or a runner who notches up wins has recorded them.

entries.clue: On which line’s dropped by Pole with spade? (8)

blocks.note: a spade is one kind of playing card

annotation.surface: A Polish man with a shovel, and a fishing line let fall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is the wooden sort. To drop someone a line is to send a short note, and a postcard is where it goes.
annotation.definitionFit: A postcard is something on which you drop a friend a line.

indicatorNotes.in: the unknown and soldiers go inside the mass

blocks.note: a pat is a small mass, as of butter
algebra's unknown; inside PAT after PA

annotation.surface: An army of unnamed troops pushing forward en masse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Advance' looks military, matching the soldiers, but is the money kind, paid up front.
annotation.definitionFit: An advance is a payment made before it is due, hence the question mark.

indicatorNotes.opens: the lunchtime worker opens up the energy, getting inside it

blocks.note: chi = life energy in Chinese thought
one o'clock, I in Roman numerals; goes after CH

annotation.surface: An office worker at lunch cracking open a can of energy drink.
annotation.walkthrough: Lunchtime is one o'clock, hence I. The pair IANT splits CHI between H and I.
annotation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany.

entries.clue: Cruelty of Ohio judge upset Columbus? (8)

blocks.note: O is a dictionary abbreviation for Ohio
Columbus, Ohio's capital, is one example of a city

annotation.surface: An American judge who was brutal and angered the state capital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Columbus' suggests the explorer, but next to Ohio it is the state capital, standing for any city; the question mark admits the example.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: fierceness and savagery shade into cruelty, as in the ferocity of an attack.

indicatorNotes.unpacked: the outer wrapping taken off, first and last letters removed

annotation.surface: A granny unboxing her new espresso machine.
annotation.walkthrough: The coffee-maker is the person, a barista, not an appliance. The question mark signals that a lady is one example of an aristocrat.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a titled woman such as Lady Mary is one kind of aristocrat, shortened informally here.

entries.clue: One with wind steps out of line (5)

indicatorNotes.out of: the line letter is taken out

annotation.surface: A flatulent person marching out of step in a parade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wind' is read as the verb rhyming with find: a snake winds its way. L for line is a standard abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: An adder is a snake, a creature that winds as it moves.

entries.clue: A bend hiker negotiated in town (10)

indicatorNotes.negotiated: worked through, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A walker getting round a corner on the way into town.
annotation.walkthrough: Birkenhead is a town on the Wirral, across the Mersey from Liverpool.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: this Wirral port facing Liverpool across the Mersey is one English town among many.

entries.clue: Potty or bowl over on the counter? (4)

blocks.note: to bowl someone over is to stun them

annotation.surface: A shopper wondering whether the bowl of snacks on the bar is nuts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the counter' conjures a shop or bar, and nuts do sit there; it means backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Potty and nuts both mean crazy.

entries.clue: Yank in corporation getting a rise (3)

indicatorNotes.getting a rise: in a down clue, rising means reading upward

blocks.note: corporation is old British slang for a paunch

annotation.surface: An American employee in a big company earning a pay rise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American but is the verb, to pull. Corporation as a big belly is dated British humour.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: both mean to pull sharply and hard, as on a rope or a sleeve.

blocks.note: the verb: how a cat takes milk, with its tongue

annotation.surface: Buying rounds of drinks at the pub.
annotation.walkthrough: A round of drinks is the British pub custom of buying for the group; here rounds are circuits and drinks is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Laps are rounds of a course, and laps also means drinks with the tongue.

entries.clue: Singer taking long look around Lima (8)

indicatorNotes.taking: a thing that takes something in, as a room takes guests, holds it inside
indicatorNotes.around: the look wraps around the L

blocks.note: a stare is a long look

annotation.surface: A vocalist gazing at the Peruvian capital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Singer' suggests a performer, but it is a songbird, and Lima is just L.
annotation.definitionFit: The starling is a bird known for its song and mimicry.
